headline: GOLD BOUNCES $44 OFF 2026 LOW TO $4,218 — RATIO 63.9 SIGNALS SILVER UNDERVALUED AS FOMC OPENS MONDAY
snippet: Gold closed Friday June 13, 2026 at $4,218.78 — a $44 recovery from the $4,174 intraday low reached mid-week, which had marked the metal's worst 2026 print since the January all-time high of $5,589. Silver held near $65 through the week, pushing the gold:silver ratio to approximately 64.9 — its highest level of 2026 and well above the long-run post-2000 average of 60–65:1, meaning silver is historically cheap relative to gold at current levels. The setup heading into FOMC week is cleanly binary: Kevin Warsh's inaugural June 16–17 Federal Reserve meeting is 97% priced for a hold, but the dot plot's signal on December rate hike odds (currently at 70%) will determine whether the $4,000–$4,218 range is a correction low or the ceiling of a new, lower trading band. For junior mining investors, the critical context is that institutional year-end gold targets have not moved despite the correction: Goldman Sachs $5,400, JPMorgan approximately $6,000, UBS $5,500, and Morgan Stanley $5,200 still sit 13–44% above current spot, implying that Wall Street's structural thesis remains intact and that the drawdown is being read as a sentiment dislocation driven by a single monetary catalyst rather than a fundamental break. The gold:silver ratio at 64+ is simultaneously the most important trading signal of the weekend: historically, every time the ratio has moved above 63 during a precious metals bull market and then contracted, silver has outperformed gold by 2–4x on the recovery leg. With the physical silver market running its sixth consecutive annual deficit, China having reclassified silver as a strategic material with export licensing requirements since January 2026, and industrial demand for solar and EV applications growing at 11%+ per year, any post-FOMC relief that re-establishes the monetary bid for precious metals is expected to hit silver disproportionately hard on the upside.

headline: ENERGY FUELS HITS FULL-YEAR URANIUM GUIDANCE IN 6 MONTHS — WHITE MESA MILL PIVOTS TO RARE EARTH NdPr IN JULY
source_name: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE: UUUU; TSX: EFR)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE: UUUU; TSX: EFR) announced June 11, 2026 that it expects to produce approximately 1.6 million pounds of finished uranium oxide (U3O8) at its White Mesa Mill in Utah by June 30 — falling within its full-year guidance range of 1.5–2.5 million pounds and representing an average monthly output pace of more than 265,000 pounds across the first six months of 2026. The ore feed comes from the Pinyon Plain mine in Arizona and the La Sal Complex in Utah, both of which have been ramping production in 2026 under the tailwind of uranium spot prices near $85–$86 per pound — approximately double the $40–$45/lb range that was standard in 2020–2022. Critically, after the current uranium ore processing campaign completes by end of June, Energy Fuels will immediately commence rare earth element (REE) circuit modifications at White Mesa — the only fully licensed uranium and REE processing facility in the United States — to expand the Phase 1 NdPr (neodymium-praseodymium) separated product capacity that is already delivering commercial quantities. This dual-commodity pivot is strategically significant: Energy Fuels is positioning White Mesa as the only facility in the Western Hemisphere that can process both uranium and separated rare earth products at commercial scale, with NdPr specifically being the rare earth magnet material facing the most acute supply chain pressure from China's export licensing regime and the G7's push for Western supply chain independence. For uranium investors on the TSXV and NYSE, Energy Fuels' ahead-of-schedule guidance achievement — in a market where most operators have historically missed production targets — is the sector's strongest H1 2026 operational data point, and the REE pivot adds a second commodity revenue stream that the market has not yet fully valued at current uranium-centric multiples.

headline: COPPER SLIDES TO 3-WEEK LOW AT $13,378/t — MIDDLE EAST ESCALATION UNDERCUTS GOLDMAN/CITI BULLISH CALL
snippet: Benchmark three-month LME copper fell 0.75% to $13,414.50 per tonne on June 11, 2026, touching an intraday low of $13,378 — a fresh three-week low — as escalating Middle East conflict raised fears of oil-driven inflation tightening global monetary policy and slowing industrial demand growth. The Shanghai Futures Exchange most-traded contract simultaneously fell 1.5% to 102,910 yuan per tonne, signalling that Chinese demand-side concerns compounded the Western geopolitical risk premium in a single session. The move is notable because it runs directly against the simultaneous bullish positions of Goldman Sachs (which raised its year-end copper target to $13,735/t and widened its ex-US supply deficit forecast to 640,000 tonnes) and Citigroup (which turned bullish for the first time in 2026, targeting $14,500/t in June and $15,000/t within 12 months). The divergence — banks bullish on structural supply disruptions at Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula, but the spot market selling on geopolitical risk — is exactly the environment that has historically produced volatile copper price moves in both directions within short windows. For retail investors in TSXV copper developers, the key distinction is that the Goldman and Citi bullish cases rest on supply disruption fundamentals (not demand), meaning a Middle East-driven demand fear selloff is potentially temporary noise against a structural signal. Copper is on track for its third consecutive weekly decline as of June 11, having been pushed down by the combination of FOMC uncertainty weighing on all industrial metals, Middle East conflict elevating energy inflation expectations, and profit-taking from earlier 2026 highs above $14,000/t.

headline: TIMMINS TRIPLE-HIT: METALS CREEK OGDEN COMPLETES 3-HOLE DRILL WITH VISIBLE GOLD IN ALL HOLES — ASSAYS PENDING
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Metals Creek Resources (TSXV: MEK)
snippet: Metals Creek Resources Corp. (TSXV: MEK) announced June 11, 2026 that its third and final drill hole of the 2026 program at the Ogden Gold Project in Timmins, Ontario returned visible gold at 350.36 metres depth within strongly altered felsite near the Thomas Ogden Zone fold axis — completing a program in which all three holes returned visible gold in core. The Ogden JV is a 50/50 joint venture with Discovery Silver Corp. (TSX: DSV), with Metals Creek serving as the operator; the project targets the lower portion of the Thomas Ogden Zone fold structure, which has a shallow easterly plunge consistent with other high-grade Timmins camp gold systems. Visible gold at greater than 350 metres depth in Timmins camp felsite near a known fold axis is a meaningful visual result because the Thomas Ogden Zone's high-grade mineralization is structurally controlled — the fold axis geometry drives grade concentration, and a visual hit within the fold axis at that depth confirms the team is drilling on the right structural target. All assay results from the three-hole program are pending and expected over the coming weeks. For speculative junior gold investors, a fully drilled three-hole program with 100% visual gold intercepts in a Timmins camp setting — the highest-grade district average in Canadian gold mining history — is the setup that typically drives a de-risking re-rating in small-cap explorers when assays are reported, particularly at $4,200/oz gold and with joint venture validation from a credible mid-tier partner in Discovery Silver.

headline: NOA LITHIUM: TWO RIGS DRILLING RIO GRANDE BRINE IN ARGENTINA — PFS ON SCHEDULE FOR YEAR-END 2026
source_name: Junior Mining Network / NOA Lithium Brines (TSXV: NOAL)
snippet: NOA Lithium Brines Inc. (TSXV: NOAL) reported June 11, 2026 that both drilling rigs are operating as planned at the Rio Grande lithium brine project in Salta Province, Argentina, with Well RT-RG26-PW001 reaching 168 metres and Well RT-RG26-PW002 reaching 30 metres — progressing on schedule toward the company's targeted Preliminary Feasibility Study completion by year-end 2026. The Rio Grande project is a lithium brine asset in the Argentinian Puna plateau — the same geological setting as Lithium Americas' Cauchari-Olaroz operation and SQM's Atacama — which targets lithium-bearing brines in salar (salt flat) aquifers rather than the hard rock pegmatite deposits that dominate the James Bay corridor. Lithium brine projects typically have lower production costs than hardrock or spodumene-based projects (due to solar evaporation rather than crushing and flotation), but carry distinct Argentine political and economic risk, including Milei administration economic reforms and currency policy uncertainty. Argentina under President Milei has moved aggressively to deregulate the mining sector and attract foreign investment, with a special mining investment regime (RIGI) passed in 2024 that provides tax stability and foreign exchange guarantees for qualifying projects above $200M — meaningfully reducing the political risk discount that Argentine mining assets carried in prior administrations. For retail investors tracking the full lithium supply landscape, NOA's Rio Grande brine progress is the South American counterpart to the James Bay hardrock stories dominating Canadian headlines, and at $26,278/t lithium carbonate (Q1 2026 average), brine projects with advancing feasibility studies are beginning to attract development capital from battery manufacturers seeking non-Chinese, non-DRC supply chain diversification.

headline: DOUBLEVIEW GOLD HAT: 8m AT 4.04 g/t Au IN NEW FAR EAST ZONE — 150m STEP-OUT BEYOND BC RESOURCE BOUNDARY
snippet: Doubleview Gold Corp. (TSXV: DBG) reported June 9, 2026 assay results from drill holes H102–H108 at the Hat Polymetallic Project in northwestern British Columbia, opening a new Far East Zone approximately 150 metres east of the current mineral resource envelope. Key intersections from the program include 8.0 metres grading 4.04 g/t gold — a high-grade gold-enriched intercept approximately 150 metres beyond the MRE boundary — along with longer, lower-grade intervals of 693.0 metres at 0.20% CuEq (H102) and 531.0 metres at 0.20% CuEq (H103), confirming that bulk-tonnage copper-gold-cobalt mineralisation extends to and through the Far East Zone contact. These holes post-date the Hat February 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate and the March 2026 Preliminary Economic Assessment, meaning the Far East Zone was not incorporated in either study and represents incremental ounces above what the PEA modelled as the mine plan. For investors tracking the BC polymetallic sector, the Hat project's combined profile — a large tonnage copper-cobalt-gold-platinum system with bulk tonnage drilling intercepts over hundreds of metres, a completed PEA, and now a step-out discovery adding a gold-enriched eastern zone — fits the template of northwestern BC deposits that strategic acquirers have sought for their critical mineral diversity and proximity to Pacific coast export infrastructure. A 4.04 g/t Au interval in a broadly gold-copper system is economically significant because higher-grade gold subzones within a bulk deposit can materially improve mine plan grade and strip ratio; the Far East Zone's grade relative to the average resource grade will be the key metric when Doubleview incorporates it into the next resource update.

headline: BEARISH BIAS BUILDS AHEAD OF FOMC: GOLD AND SILVER TECHNICALS FAIL TO CONFIRM FRIDAY'S BOUNCE
snippet: Forex.com's pre-FOMC technical analysis published June 12–13, 2026 argues that despite gold's Friday bounce to $4,218, the technical picture for both gold and silver heading into Warsh's inaugural June 16–17 FOMC remains bearish: gold is trading below key moving averages in momentum terms, silver is pinned near $65 with declining relative strength against the broader commodity complex, and the consensus 97% probability of a June hold does not remove the hawkish risk embedded in the dot plot for the second half of 2026. The core bearish argument is that the FOMC's dot plot — the first since March 2026 and the first under Warsh's leadership — will either confirm the 70% December hike odds that markets are pricing or fail to push back against them meaningfully, and either outcome is less supportive than what gold needs to break decisively above $4,400 resistance. The most important technical level the piece identifies is the $4,150–$4,175 support zone: gold has now held this area through multiple tests (intraday low $4,174), and a close below it on FOMC week would be the technical signal that the $4,000 psychological level becomes the next significant target. For junior mining investors interpreting this setup: the bearish case is FOMC-conditional and monetarily driven, not fundamentally driven — which means a dot-plot surprise that signals Warsh is more cautious about the inflationary impact of rate hikes on a heavily indebted economy could flip the technical picture sharply, making the risk-reward on gold and silver junior positions asymmetrically positive if held through the FOMC binary.

headline: G7 LEADERS ARRIVE AT ÉVIAN SUNDAY — CHINA'S 90% RARE EARTH LOCK IS THE STRATEGIC MINING REALITY THEY MUST CONFRONT
snippet: G7 leaders begin arriving at Évian-les-Bains, France on Sunday June 14, 2026 ahead of the formal summit June 15–17, with the Atlantic Council's pre-summit analysis identifying China's concentrated control of critical minerals processing as the single most consequential structural challenge the G7 must address. China controls approximately 90% of global rare earth element processing, 80% of battery-grade graphite processing, and 70% of battery-grade manganese processing — supply chain concentration points that China's Q2 2026 rare earth concentrate price increase of approximately 45% has already demonstrated can be used as economic leverage independent of direct tariff retaliation. The specific G7 deliverable that mining investors should track is not the headline communiqué but rather the fine print: whether the permanent critical minerals secretariat announced at Évian will have the authority to co-ordinate government-backed offtake agreements and strategic reserve purchases for Western-produced critical minerals, or whether it will remain a co-ordination body without binding procurement power. The difference is transformative for junior critical mineral project economics: binding government offtake at a floor price removes the single most significant financing obstacle — commercial offtake agreements — that has stalled development of rare earth, graphite, manganese, lithium, and nickel projects in Australia, Canada, and the US despite technically advanced project definitions. For TSXV and ASX investors, the Évian summit represents the policy inflection point that determines whether the G7 critical mineral supply chain ambitions of 2022–2026 will finally translate into committed capital that funds project development, or whether they remain aspirational frameworks subject to annual re-endorsement without procurement follow-through.

headline: GOLD PULLBACK JUNE 2026: IS THIS THE BUYING WINDOW OR A DEEPER TRAP? CMR BREAKS DOWN THE CASE FOR EACH
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's June 2026 analysis of the gold correction asks the question that every junior mining investor is wrestling with heading into FOMC week: is the pullback from gold's $5,589 January all-time high to the current $4,218 range a textbook 'buy the fear' setup, or is the May CPI data (4.2%), higher-for-longer rate narrative, and Warsh's hawkish reputation creating conditions for another leg down toward $4,000 or below? The bullish case rests on four pillars: (1) every major bank's year-end 2026 target still sits 13–44% above current spot with no downward revisions, implying analysts view the correction as temporary; (2) gold's correction from ATH to current levels (24.6%) is within the normal 20–35% range for corrective phases in prior precious metals bull cycles — the 1974–1976 correction was 49% and then gold added 750% to the upside; (3) central bank buying at 850+ tonnes in 2025 continues through the correction (PBOC's 19th straight monthly purchase in May), confirming structural demand is not price-sensitive; and (4) the GDX/GDXJ drawdown of 13–15% from 2026 highs has pushed junior gold developers well below replacement cost and toward NAV discounts unseen since 2022, creating the precise acquisition window that senior producers have historically exploited. The bearish case is simpler: inflation at 4.2% with a new Fed Chair with unambiguous hawkish credentials means the monetary headwind that topped gold's run is not yet fully removed, and another hot macro print (June CPI in mid-July) could re-extend the correction beyond what structurally bullish investors expect. For retail investors, CMR argues the risk-reward favours maintaining core positions through the FOMC binary while keeping dry powder for a post-meeting confirmation either direction.

headline: 3 RARE EARTH STOCKS TO WATCH AS G7 MEETS AND WASHINGTON DOUBLES DOWN ON CHINA SUPPLY CHAIN INDEPENDENCE
snippet: Barchart's June 2026 analysis identifies three rare earth stocks positioned to benefit from Washington's accelerating push to de-risk critical mineral supply chains from China, timed to coincide with the G7 Évian summit (June 15–17) where a permanent critical minerals secretariat and potential government offtake frameworks are expected to be announced. The backdrop for all three companies is a China rare earth price increase of approximately 45% in Q2 2026 — a deliberate leverage move by Beijing amid US-China trade negotiations — which simultaneously raises the economic case for Western alternatives and reduces the cost disadvantage that non-Chinese rare earth producers have historically struggled to overcome on a pure unit-cost basis. The companies highlighted operate across the rare earth value chain: upstream mining (with Mountain Pass, California, still the only large-scale integrated rare earth mine in the US), midstream separation and processing (where the US has almost no domestic capacity outside of MP Materials' facility and the Energy Fuels White Mesa REE circuit), and downstream magnet manufacturing (where USA Rare Earth's Less Common Metals acquisition gives it UK refining capacity). For junior rare earth investors on the TSXV and ASX, the critical read-through from Washington's policy escalation is that government-backed Western buyers — US DOD, European industrial purchasers, Japanese battery makers — are becoming the primary off-takers for advanced rare earth projects, displacing the commercial export contracts to Chinese processors that had been the historical financing mechanism for junior HREE and LREE explorers. This policy shift means projects with defined resources in Tier 1 jurisdictions that can qualify for DOD or G7 secretariat procurement are approaching a financing de-risking event that is independent of the commercial rare earth market cycle.
